lessons.title: Facial mechanics
lessons.objective: Learn to see individual facial movements before assigning emotion.
lessons.source_note: FACS-inspired; not a clinical coding exercise.

groups.title: Brows
groups.invariants: Keep eyes, lips and head angle neutral.

groups.title: Eyes and cheeks
groups.invariants: Keep eyebrows and mouth unchanged where anatomically possible.

groups.title: Nose and upper lip
groups.invariants: Keep head and gaze fixed.

groups.title: Mouth
groups.invariants: Keep brows and gaze neutral.

lessons.title: Basic emotional expressions
lessons.objective: Recognize common expression families without treating them as universal diagnoses.
lessons.source_note: GoEmotions and EMOTIC inspired; curated examples.

groups.title: Positive affect
groups.invariants: Same frontal framing and direct gaze.

groups.title: Negative affect
groups.invariants: Same framing; expression only.

groups.title: Attention and surprise
groups.invariants: No symbols, props or lighting changes.

lessons.title: Complex and mixed emotions
lessons.objective: Show emotional distinctions with subtle facial cues.
lessons.source_note: GoEmotions-inspired; cues are artistic choices, not diagnostic rules.

groups.title: Self-conscious emotions
groups.invariants: Do not change camera or costume.

groups.title: Social emotions
groups.invariants: Same neutral background; no second person.

groups.title: Inner conflict
groups.invariants: Show ambiguity without text or icons.

lessons.title: Emotional intensity and concealment
lessons.objective: Distinguish degree from type and outer display from inner feeling.
lessons.source_note: Curated intensity ladders.

groups.title: Anger ladder
groups.invariants: Keep head angle and lighting fixed.

groups.title: Joy ladder
groups.invariants: Keep face orientation fixed.

groups.title: Fear ladder
groups.invariants: Keep head orientation fixed.

groups.title: Sadness ladder
groups.invariants: No rain or added lighting.

groups.title: Masking emotion
groups.invariants: No caption or thought bubble in the render.

lessons.title: Gaze and attention
lessons.objective: Use eye direction and head orientation to imply intention.
lessons.source_note: Curated staging studies.

groups.title: Eye direction
groups.invariants: Head fixed frontally; move only pupils.

groups.title: Head orientation
groups.invariants: Maintain neutral expression.

groups.title: Attention in context
groups.invariants: Keep café geometry and cup position fixed.

lessons.title: Body language
lessons.objective: Understand posture as an expressive signal rather than a fixed diagnosis.
lessons.source_note: Danbooru posture vocabulary and curated acting cues.

groups.title: Openness and confidence
groups.invariants: Same full-body frame and floor marks.

groups.title: Defensive and vulnerable
groups.invariants: Neutral face, same costume.

groups.title: Energy and weight
groups.invariants: No environmental changes.

groups.title: Status contrast
groups.invariants: Same camera height; no size distortion.

lessons.title: Gestures and hands
lessons.objective: Show the communicative function of hands and culturally contextual gestures.
lessons.source_note: Danbooru gesture categories; cultural interpretations must be contextualized.

groups.title: Social gestures
groups.invariants: Same full-body framing and neutral face.

groups.title: Thinking and speaking
groups.invariants: Hands remain anatomically plausible.

groups.title: Emblematic gestures
groups.invariants: Use the described gesture without asserting universal meaning.

lessons.title: Action and implied motion
lessons.objective: Learn to depict verbs and stages of movement in still pictures.
lessons.source_note: Danbooru action vocabulary; curated motion studies.

groups.title: Café verbs
groups.invariants: Same café furniture, camera and cup design; pose may change.

groups.title: Locomotion
groups.invariants: Same backdrop and full-body crop.

groups.title: Action phases
groups.invariants: Use an imaginary light ball; fixed camera and consistent floor.

lessons.title: Interpersonal relationships
lessons.objective: Show social relationships through coordinated behavior.
lessons.source_note: Danbooru interaction vocabulary; curated relationship studies.

groups.title: Affiliation
groups.invariants: Same two identities, chairs and table; expressions and posture may change.

groups.title: Conflict
groups.invariants: No violence or props beyond agreed café items.

groups.title: Social hierarchy
groups.invariants: Keep camera eye level; use behavior rather than scale.

lessons.title: Proxemics and blocking
lessons.objective: Explore distance, orientation, and shared attention.
lessons.source_note: Curated staging; distance norms vary by culture and context.

groups.title: Distance
groups.invariants: Use a fixed wider crop with movable chairs and identical table.

groups.title: Orientation
groups.invariants: Keep both chairs at the same distance from each other.

groups.title: Attention triangle
groups.invariants: Same wafer on tabletop and same seating.

lessons.title: Subtext and contradiction
lessons.objective: Distinguish visible behavior from implied private intention.
lessons.source_note: Curated acting and visual-narrative examples.

groups.title: Same words different delivery
groups.invariants: The page supplies identical dialogue: Thank you. Do not render lettering.

groups.title: Same smile different context
groups.invariants: TSMC keeps a small polite smile; change only context and companion reaction.

groups.title: Face versus body
groups.invariants: Same full-body framing.

lessons.title: Manga visual vocabulary
lessons.objective: Learn conventional drawn signs, separate from realistic acting.
lessons.source_note: Cohn and Ehly manga morphology inspired; original illustrations.

groups.title: Emotion signs
groups.invariants: Keep base facial pixels if possible; add only the visual sign.

groups.title: Cognitive and physical signs
groups.invariants: Use original graphic marks; no speech bubbles.

groups.title: Motion signs
groups.invariants: Use fixed action pose derived from lesson 8; vary only graphic marks.

lessons.title: Atmosphere and emotional context
lessons.objective: See how story cues change mood even under fixed light and color.
lessons.source_note: Curated mood studies; Part 2 owns lighting recipes.

groups.title: Café atmosphere
groups.invariants: Keep original daylight and camera; vary story evidence only.

groups.title: Same mood different cues
groups.invariants: Target loneliness in every image; lighting fixed.

lessons.title: Props and environmental storytelling
lessons.objective: Use objects and traces to imply events without showing them.
lessons.source_note: Iconclass and Visual Genome inspired; original scenes.

groups.title: One changed prop
groups.invariants: Cup, pose, camera, light and furniture fixed; change tabletop clue.

groups.title: Evidence of past events
groups.invariants: Do not change daylight or camera; use environmental traces.

lessons.title: Symbols and cultural meaning
lessons.objective: Learn conventional, contextual and invented symbols without claiming universality.
lessons.source_note: Iconclass and Chinese Iconography Thesaurus inspired; verify cultural notes separately.

groups.title: Objects as symbols
groups.invariants: Same character posture and simple stage; one symbolic object.

groups.title: Cultural contextual examples
groups.invariants: Keep costume canonical; add object, not a new historical style.

groups.title: Invented Silicon Wars symbols
groups.invariants: Do not add words or logos beyond canon.

lessons.title: Visual rhetoric and metaphor
lessons.objective: Communicate abstract claims through visual relationships.
lessons.source_note: VisMet and MetaCLUE inspired; original metaphors.

groups.title: Metaphorical constructions
groups.invariants: Same neutral rendering; permit impossible objects.

groups.title: Rhetorical intentions
groups.invariants: Illustrate concept; page explains alternative readings.

groups.title: One idea multiple metaphors
groups.invariants: Target dependency in every image.

lessons.title: Narrative moments
lessons.objective: Recognize the role a single picture plays within an event.
lessons.source_note: Cohn visual narrative grammar inspired; terms adapted pedagogically.

groups.title: The mysterious envelope
groups.invariants: Same envelope, room, costume and fixed wide camera.

groups.title: Before or after
groups.invariants: Same props and camera; each image is a distinct instant.

lessons.title: Sequential visual grammar
lessons.objective: Learn how panel selection and order create inference.
lessons.source_note: Cohn visual narrative grammar; curated continuity exercises.

groups.title: Cup accident
groups.invariants: Fixed camera and identical cup; no lettering.

groups.title: The discovery
groups.invariants: Fixed camera and same envelope.

groups.title: Parallel actions
groups.invariants: Same two characters and props; preserve screen positions.

groups.title: Ellipsis and inference
groups.invariants: Same doorway and envelope; middle panel optional on page.

groups.title: Reaction cut
groups.invariants: Camera may cut between approved eye-line matched medium shots.

lessons.title: Genre and narrative framing
lessons.objective: Use the same premise to create different genre expectations without changing art style.
lessons.source_note: Curated narrative genres; no copying specific films.

groups.title: One envelope six genres
groups.invariants: Keep neutral digital painting and daylight; change plot cues, not rendering.

groups.title: Archetypal roles
groups.invariants: Same outfit, camera and style; demonstrate role through action and prop.

lessons.title: Integration and visual critique
lessons.objective: Practice communicating an intention and diagnosing why images fail.
lessons.source_note: Original capstone; some cards deliberately vary multiple variables.

groups.title: Same visual brief three approaches
groups.invariants: Target anticipation; each solution changes a different channel.

groups.title: Clear versus unclear
groups.invariants: Target reconciliation; deliberately produce an instructive failure.

groups.title: Final story
groups.invariants: Same café and fixed screen direction; multi-variable capstone.

lessons.title: Semantic experiment A — Same meaning, different implementation
lessons.objective: Show that one intended meaning can be built from many different visual mechanisms.
lessons.source_note: Supplementary semantic experiments (2026-11-26); mechanisms cross-reference Part II.

groups.title: Loneliness, four ways
groups.invariants: The intended meaning (loneliness) stays fixed; the visual mechanism changes.

groups.title: Authority, four ways
groups.invariants: The intended meaning (authority) stays fixed; the visual mechanism changes.

groups.title: Suspense, four ways
groups.invariants: The intended meaning (suspense) stays fixed; the visual mechanism changes.

groups.title: Hope, four ways
groups.invariants: The intended meaning (hope) stays fixed; the visual mechanism changes.

groups.title: Vulnerability, four ways
groups.invariants: The intended meaning (vulnerability) stays fixed; the visual mechanism changes.

lessons.title: Semantic experiment B — Same visual element, different meanings
lessons.objective: Show that visual elements have no fixed universal meaning; context decides.
lessons.source_note: Supplementary semantic experiments (2026-11-26).

groups.title: Red, four meanings
groups.invariants: The element (red) stays; context changes its meaning.

groups.title: Darkness, four meanings
groups.invariants: The element (darkness) stays; context changes its meaning.

groups.title: An empty chair, four meanings
groups.invariants: The element (an empty chair) stays; context changes its meaning.

groups.title: A smile, four meanings
groups.invariants: The element (a smile) stays; context changes its meaning.

lessons.title: Semantic experiment C — Same image, different context
lessons.objective: Show that meaning can come from outside the picture: the same image reads differently under different captions.
lessons.source_note: Supplementary semantic experiments (2026-11-26); images reused unchanged.

groups.title: One picture, three stories
groups.invariants: The picture never changes; only the page-rendered caption changes.

C00: She arrived thirty minutes early for their first meeting.
It was the first morning she returned to their favorite café alone.
After ten years of work, she could finally sit down and rest.
C04: The letter she had waited months for was finally here.
She already knew what was inside, and it would change nothing.
Someone had left it on the wrong table — it was never meant for her.
l05-g03-v04: She was rehearsing exactly what she would say when he arrived.
She had just decided to leave the company she had built her life around.
Her tea had gone cold an hour ago; she had not noticed.
l13-g01-v04: The photograph showed the café's first day, forty years ago.
She kept the photo of the friend who would not be coming back.
She found it inside a second-hand book and wondered who they were.

lessons.title: Semantic experiment D — Same scene, different narrative intent
lessons.objective: Show that genre lives in behavior, props and emphasis — not in a style filter.
lessons.source_note: Supplementary semantic experiments (2026-11-26).

groups.title: One meeting, five genres
groups.invariants: Same café two-shot: TSMC screen left, ASML screen right, meeting at the table. Change behavior, props and emphasis only — never the rendering style or color grade.

lessons.title: Semantic experiment E — Intended vs perceived meaning
lessons.objective: Practice interpreting an image before the intended meaning is revealed, and see why viewers disagree.
lessons.source_note: Supplementary semantic experiments (2026-11-26); quiz mode supported.
